official.deadline_note: No single deadline exists. DAAD's official list of application deadlines for intake 2027/2028 (Stand 06/2026) answers 'see website of the course' for every listed course, and DAAD states 'Depending on chosen study programme; please check ... the website of your chosen study programme.' Deadlines differ per course: the University of Oldenburg's SuRE course, for example, publishes 15 October 2026 for DAAD EPOS applicants from developing countries (regular deadline 15 January 2027). DAAD's FAQ confirms that if a course deadline has passed you cannot still apply.
official.application_cycle: Intake 2027/2028 (DAAD deadlines list ST42 - EPOS Deadlines, Stand 06/2026)
official.status_note: The programme is running for the 2027/2028 intake; DAAD's current deadlines list (Stand 06/2026) covers course applications for that intake and each course runs its own window and selection committee. DAAD notes that the majority of the selection process will be finished in March, and the programme page states that scholarship calls are subject to funds being made available by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
official.tuition_coverage_note: DAAD's official EPOS FAQ (Stand 06/2026): 'You do not pay for the tuition fees, but there may be registration or enrollment fees you have to pay. Please contact the university.'
official.funding_period: per month (EUR 992 graduates / 1,400 PhD from Feb 2026)
benefits: Depending on academic level, monthly payments of 992 euros for graduates or 1,300 euros (1,400 euros beginning with February 2026) for doctoral candidates
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless these expenses are covered by the home country or another source of funding
Under certain circumstances: monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying members of family
For courses taught in German, the scholarship includes a preparatory six-month German language course in Germany
eligibility: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from the countries on DAAD's list of eligible countries (DAC list)

Works either for a public authority or a state or private company in a developing country, engaged in the planning and execution of directives and projects with emphasis on development policies with a bearing on technological, economic or social areas
Holds a Bachelor's degree (normally four years) in a related subject, completed with far above average results (upper third)
At least two years of related professional experience after the first degree (bachelor) at the time of application; academic degrees should normally not be more than six years old

Candidates can prove their motivation is development-related and be expected to take on social responsibility and initiate and support processes of change in their personal and professional environment
Applicants who have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered
requirements: Applications have only to be sent to the respective course directly; applications sent to the DAAD will not be forwarded to the course/university
The complete application has to be submitted in English or German to be considered; incomplete applications cannot be considered

You can apply for up to three courses, listed in order of priority in the DAAD application form (section 7. Choice of host university/institution in Germany), and you must apply to each of the chosen universities directly

When applying to more than one course, one uniform letter of motivation must explain the choice of courses and the prioritisation; if this is ignored the application cannot be considered or an awarded scholarship might be withdrawn
If shortlisted there will be a telephone interview with the university staff, which may only be conducted by the applicant
Keep a copy of every document, because the complete application must be uploaded as PDFs to the DAAD Portal if you are suggested for a DAAD scholarship
documents: Completed and signed EPOS checklist plus the EPOS application form (typed answers)
Curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order without any unexplained gaps, using the Europass template
One letter of motivation with detailed reference to academic, professional and personal reasons for applying for the programme
Letter of recommendation from your current employer, on official letterhead with signature and official stamp and of current date (not in a sealed envelope)

Certificate(s) of employment showing at least two years of relevant work experience after the Bachelor's degree up to the time of application, ideally including a guarantee of re-employment after returning to the home country
Recent proof of language skills - English: IELTS or TOEFL (the institutional TOEFL is not accepted); German: required for courses taught in German

Copies of higher education degree certificates and the full set of transcripts of records, with certified translation if the original is not in German or English and an explanation of the grading system if not part of the transcript; applicants from the People's Republic of China are asked to submit an APS Certificate
selection_criteria: Candidates fulfil the necessary academic requirements and can be expected to successfully complete a study programme in Germany (above-average result for first academic exam - top performance third, language skills)
Candidates have a Bachelor degree (usually a four-year course) in an appropriate subject
Candidates have at least two years of professional experience
Candidates can prove their motivation is development-related and be expected to take on social responsibility and initiate and support processes of change after their training/scholarship
A selection committee at the course suggests potential candidates for a DAAD scholarship; shortlisted candidates face a telephone interview with university staff
coverage: Monthly payments of 992 euros for graduates or 1,300 euros (1,400 euros beginning with February 2026) for doctoral candidates
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless these expenses are covered by the home country or another source of funding
Under certain circumstances, monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying members of family
application_method: Step 1: you send your complete application directly to the postgraduate course of your choice (maximum three, ranked by priority)
Step 2: a selection committee suggests potential candidates for a DAAD scholarship
Step 3: the suggested candidates are contacted by DAAD to upload their complete application to the DAAD Portal
Step 4: the selection process is finalised and the suggested candidates are informed accordingly
official.application_route: Apply directly to the chosen course (never to DAAD), through that course's own online or postal application procedure by its published deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be graduates of the countries on DAAD's list of eligible countries (DAC list) for EPOS; DAAD defines country as the country in which you are living and from which you are applying, and states that applicants resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is exclusively for graduates from development and newly industrialised countries on the DAAD DAC list; long-term residents of Germany (>15 months at the application deadline) are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Individual scholarships exclusively for postgraduate courses in Germany that are listed on the DAAD's List of all Postgraduate Courses with application deadlines 2027/2028; the scholarship is only granted for the entire duration of a listed course, and applicants may target a maximum of three courses. Funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
official.description: With its development-oriented postgraduate study programmes, the DAAD promotes the training of specialists from development and newly industrialised countries: the scholarships offer foreign graduates from those countries, from all disciplines and with at least two years' professional experience, the chance to take a postgraduate or Master's degree at a state or state-recognised German university and, in exceptional cases, to take a doctoral degree.
official.program_type: Development-related postgraduate scholarship (EPOS): individual scholarships for listed Master's courses in Germany, exceptionally doctoral degrees
official.english_requirement: For courses in English: proof of adequate language skills according to the regulations of the respective course; DAAD's required documents specify a recent IELTS or TOEFL score and state that the institutional TOEFL is not accepted. For courses taught in German: DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 must be passed before the start of the study course, and a minimum German level of B1 at the time of application is required.

not_confirmed: deadline_central - DAAD publishes no single deadline; its official deadlines list for intake 2027/2028 says 'see website of the course' for every course
exact per-course deadlines and course-specific additional documents (each course's own website governs)
the full list of eligible countries (published by DAAD as a separate DAC-list PDF)
verification.notes: Funding amount, currency, period, benefits, eligibility, documents, requirements and the four-step application procedure were taken from DAAD's own EPOS scholarship database entry; the tuition/fee position, the three-course rule, the language rules and the shortlisting interview come from DAAD's official EPOS FAQ; the 2027/2028 cycle comes from DAAD's official deadlines list; the concrete deadline example comes from the University of Oldenburg's own SuRE course page.

applicant_utility.summary: EPOS is not an application to DAAD: you apply straight to one of the roughly thirty listed postgraduate courses (maximum three), and each course runs its own deadline and selection committee, so your first real task is picking the right course and meeting its date - for the 2027/2028 intake those fall in autumn 2026 (Oldenburg's SuRE course, for instance, sets 15 October 2026 for DAAD EPOS applicants). Funding is a monthly stipend of EUR 992 at graduate level (EUR 1,300, rising to EUR 1,400 from February 2026, for doctoral candidates) plus insurance payments and a travel allowance, and DAAD's own FAQ confirms you do not pay tuition on the listed courses, although registration or enrolment fees remain yours. Eligibility turns on being a national of a DAAD DAC-list country, holding a normally four-year bachelor's in a related subject, at least two years of relevant post-bachelor professional experience, upper-third results, degrees no older than six years, and no more than 15 months' residence in Germany at the application deadline. Because you need an employer recommendation letter and employment certificates, those documents should be lined up months before the course deadline, not weeks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from DAC-list countries with a relevant four-year bachelor's, two-plus years of development-sector work experience, and an employer willing to recommend them and guarantee re-employment on return home.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on DAAD's EPOS list of eligible countries and that your chosen course appears in the current 2027/2028 deadlines list before you invest time in documents.
Open each target course's own website and note its exact EPOS deadline plus any course-specific extra documents; the DAAD booklet is not the final word on what a course requires.
Request the employer recommendation letter early - it must be on official letterhead, with signature and official stamp, of current date and not sealed in an envelope.
Book IELTS or TOEFL early: the institutional TOEFL is not accepted, and German-taught courses additionally require at least B1 at application.

Draft one uniform letter of motivation covering all chosen courses and your ranking, and check that your degrees are less than six years old and that you have not lived in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline.
common_rejection_risks: Sending the application to DAAD instead of the course: DAAD states applications sent to it are not forwarded, so the file never reaches the selection committee.

Submitting different motivation letters, or changing your course priorities, across the three applications - DAAD warns the application cannot be considered or an awarded scholarship might be withdrawn.
Missing employment certificates proving at least two years of relevant work after the bachelor's, or an out-of-date recommendation letter.
Unexplained gaps in the Europass CV, which the documents require to be reverse-chronological without gaps.
Degrees older than six years or a three-year bachelor's, which rule the application out regardless of other strengths.
Applicants from the People's Republic of China applying without an APS certificate.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Registration/enrolment fees at the host university, which DAAD explicitly says you still have to pay, plus anything beyond the monthly stipend: the travel allowance is withheld if your home country or another funder already covers travel, and the rent subsidy and family allowance are only granted 'under certain circumstances'.
document_audit: Employer recommendation letter: letterhead, signature, official stamp, current date, not in a sealed envelope - these formalities are spelled out and are checked.
Employment certificates must show at least two years of relevant work after the bachelor's; a guarantee of re-employment after returning home is requested and should be included if possible.
Degree certificates and full transcripts need certified translations when the original is not in German or English, and an explanation of the grading system if the transcript does not include one.

For German-taught courses the scholarship includes a six-month language course in Germany, but you still need B1 at application and must pass DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before study starts - you cannot reach that level inside the intensive course alone.
Chinese applicants need the APS certificate from the German embassy's academic evaluation centre as part of the file.
alerts: Deadlines are course-specific and several fall in autumn 2026 for the October 2027 intake; DAAD's FAQ states that once a course deadline has passed you cannot still apply.
The DAAD Portal upload only happens later: if the course nominates you, DAAD contacts you to upload the complete application, so keep a PDF copy of every document from day one.
Shortlisted candidates face a telephone interview with university staff that must be conducted by the applicant personally.
The 15-month Germany residency bar is measured at the application deadline, not at the selection meeting.
Awards remain subject to BMZ funding being made available for the cycle.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply directly to each of your chosen courses (up to three, ranked) with the complete document set by that course's deadline; the course's committee nominates candidates; DAAD then asks nominees to upload the full file to the DAAD Portal and finalises the decision, with most of the selection process completed in March.

official.deadline_note: The Foundation publishes call-opening dates rather than a fixed deadline: three calls per year open on 15 March, 15 July and 15 November, and a call is closed once it has reached the maximum number of currently 800 applications. The programme page currently states that the maximum number of applications for the current call has been received, so no new applications can be created at present, and that the next call will open on 15 November 2026 (selection meeting July 2027, earliest possible fellowship start September 2027). If you cannot submit before the portal closes, your application is treated as received on the portal-closure date provided you submit no more than 14 days after the next call opens.
official.application_cycle: Three calls per year; 2026 schedule: call opens 15 March 2026 (selection November 2026, earliest start February 2027), 15 July 2026 (selection March 2027, earliest start May 2027) and 15 November 2026 (selection July 2027, earliest start September 2027)
official.status_note: The Foundation's own notice on the programme page: 'We have received the maximum number of applications for the current call. Therefore, unfortunately, no new applications can be created at present. The next call will open on November 15, 2026.' Applicants who have already started an application may save and continue working on it but cannot submit until the next round opens.
benefits: Monthly fellowship amount of EUR 3,000 for postdocs and EUR 3,600 for experienced researchers, plus additional benefits and personal support throughout the sponsorship
Mobility allowance of EUR 100 per month, paid together with each fellowship payment, as a supplement for conference attendance, research trips, archive and library visits in Germany and abroad

Subsidy towards the cost of medical and liability insurance, plus a lump sum for travel expenses and an initial subsidy; if the fellow's own institution does not cover travel expenses the Foundation pays a lump sum for return travel

Family allowance for accompanying partners and/or children under 18 staying at least three uninterrupted months: EUR 506 per month for partners, substitutional payment for child benefit of EUR 259 per child per month, and a flat-rate allowance for single-parent fellows of EUR 400 for the first child and EUR 100 for each additional child

Hosts in Germany can apply for an allowance for research costs of EUR 800 per month for research in natural sciences, life sciences and engineering, or EUR 500 per month for humanities and social sciences
An intensive German language course in Germany lasting two or four months immediately before the fellowship, including for accompanying partners
eligibility: Postdocs: doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - completed during the last four years (or completed before the envisaged selection meeting with a written summary of findings), plus publications in academic journals and by publishing houses reviewed according to international standards

Experienced researchers: doctorate completed during the last twelve years, an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and a leadership role commensurate with your career level (e.g. assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group)

If a doctorate is not possible or not customary in your field or country, you may apply for the experienced-researcher line up to 16 years after completing a master's or other postgraduate degree, provided your publication record is commensurate with your career level

You are not a German national; German nationals and 'educational residents' can apply if they have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so, or for more than five years with a strong connection to their current country of residence

You may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application; anyone who earned their living for more than 90 of those days with funding from German institutions, or worked on a doctoral project at a German institution, is not eligible
You may not apply if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation in the form of a research fellowship or research award
requirements: Applications can only be submitted online to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation; you may only submit once all required documents have been uploaded in the application form
Two expert reviews must be uploaded in a protected area by the expert reviewers personally; you can only submit once these have been uploaded, provided the portal is open at that time

Your host receives a link after submission to upload the host's statement and confirmation that research facilities are available; the application is only forwarded to the Foundation once the host has uploaded all necessary documents

Applications that fail to include important documents or information, or that diverge substantially from the specifications (e.g. for creating a list of publications), will be formally rejected without further review; ambiguities requiring clarification usually postpone the decision to the following selection meeting
The completed application form including all documents should be submitted at least four to seven months ahead of the prospective selection date
You may not apply to several Humboldt Foundation fellowship programmes concurrently; parallel applications to other funders are possible but must be declared and kept up to date
documents: Research outline (five pages maximum), with duration and any division of visits agreed with the intended host before applying
Complete list of publications following the Foundation's sample list, plus a list of selected key publications following its sample list, and the key publications themselves
Doctoral certificate or proof that the doctorate has been completed successfully, or confirmation that you will complete it before the envisaged selection meeting

German language certificate, if required; plus publisher's acceptance notifications or acknowledgements of receipt and summaries/translations of key publications not available in German or English, if required

Two expert reviews - for postdocs usually the doctoral supervisor and one other researcher, for experienced researchers important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own and other institutes
A detailed statement from your academic host in Germany together with confirmation that research facilities are available and the mentoring agreement
selection_criteria: Academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity)
Quality of the key publications named in the application (originality, innovativeness, evaluation of your own contributions to publications involving several authors)

Originality and innovative potential of your proposed research (significance for the further development of the subject area, convincing selection of methods, feasibility within the requested sponsorship period and at the host institute)
Your future potential (academic potential, personal development, career prospects)

Your independent research profile (for the experienced-researcher line); the assessment also considers your individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility
coverage: Monthly fellowship amount of EUR 3,000 (postdocs) or EUR 3,600 (experienced researchers)
Mobility allowance of EUR 100 per month for conference attendance, research trips and archive or library visits in Germany and abroad
Subsidy towards the cost of medical and liability insurance, a lump sum for travel expenses and an initial subsidy
Family benefits for accompanying partners and children, and a research-costs allowance of EUR 800 or EUR 500 per month paid to the host institute
Two- to four-month intensive German language course immediately before the fellowship, also available to accompanying partners
application_method: Submit the necessary documents to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation online only, once all required documents have been uploaded in the application form
Send the protected-area upload links to your two expert reviewers in good time; expert reviews should not be more than 12 months old at the time of application

After you submit, your host receives a link and uploads the host's statement, mentoring agreement and confirmation of research facilities; the application reaches the Foundation only once the host has completed this
After verification, a completeness check and usually two peer reviews, the application is presented to a selection committee that meets every year in March, July and November
official.application_route: Online only through the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation's application portal, with the two expert reviews and the host's statement uploaded by the reviewers and the host themselves.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to researchers of all countries excluding Germany: you must not be a German national, and German nationals or 'educational residents' (those who completed school education and a university degree, or a university degree and their doctorate, in Germany) may apply only if they have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years, or for more than five years with strong ties to their current country of residence. Applicants must have spent no more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before the application is received.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme explicitly addresses post-doctoral researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe, from all countries excluding Germany, and from any research area.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: None by discipline or country: the Foundation states there are no quotas for individual disciplines or countries, and the fellowship is open to researchers of all disciplines. Part of the Global Minds Initiative Germany of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space. A separate CAPES-Humboldt Research Fellowship exists for researchers from Brazil.
official.research_requirement: Your own research topic and host: you choose both yourself and must agree the research outline, intended duration and any division of visits with your German host before applying. A host at a research institution in Germany must supply a mentoring agreement, written confirmation that research facilities are available and a detailed review, and provide two expert reviews.
official.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months. In both cases the fellowship may be divided into a maximum of three visits, each lasting at least three months, and must be used within 36 months of commencement (48 months if extended). A 2-4 month language course immediately precedes the fellowship and is not part of it.
official.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship enables researchers of all nationalities and research areas to conduct their own research at a self-chosen host at a research institution in Germany, with a monthly fellowship amount plus additional benefits, individual support from the Foundation, and an alumni programme after the stay. The programme is part of the Global Minds Initiative Germany and expressly invites female scientists and members of underrepresented groups to apply.
official.program_type: Foundation research fellowship for postdoctoral and experienced researchers (part of the Global Minds Initiative Germany)
official.english_requirement: Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice. No language certificate is required if English or German is your native language, and an English language certificate is not required if you have worked in an English-speaking country for several years.

not_confirmed: deadline_central - the Foundation publishes call-opening dates (15 March, 15 July, 15 November) and an 800-application cap rather than a fixed deadline
tuition_coverage and fully_funded - the Foundation publishes no tuition figure for this research fellowship, so full funding cannot be asserted
the exact euro amounts of the travel-expense lump sum and the initial subsidy, which the programme information lists only as lump sums
verification.notes: Fellowship amounts, benefits, eligibility, nationality and stay rules, documents and selection criteria come from the Foundation's own programme page and its Programme information PDF (as of January 2026); the EUR 100 monthly mobility allowance and the family-benefit amounts come from the Foundation's own sponsorship-benefit pages; the current call status and 2026 calls schedule come from the notice on the programme page itself.

applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship funds a research project you design yourself, at a host institution in Germany that you choose, with EUR 3,000 per month for postdocs or EUR 3,600 for experienced researchers, plus a EUR 100 monthly mobility allowance, an insurance subsidy, a lump-sum travel payment and family allowances if partner and children accompany you for more than three months. The application is online-only and nothing reaches the Foundation until two expert reviewers and your host have uploaded their own documents, so the real bottleneck is other people's paperwork rather than your own. Timing matters twice over: calls open on 15 March, 15 July and 15 November but shut early once 800 applications arrive, and the current call is already full, so the next entry point is the call opening on 15 November 2026 for the July 2027 selection meeting (earliest fellowship start September 2027). With only about 20-25% of applications approved, the selection committee of 60-70 researchers weighs your publication record and the originality and feasibility of the five-page research outline as heavily as your career stage.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdocs within four years of their doctorate and researchers within twelve years who have publications in internationally reviewed outlets and already have a plausible German academic host in mind.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure your German host first: you need written confirmation that research facilities are available, a mentoring agreement and a detailed host statement, and the Foundation explicitly does not help you find a host.
Brief your two expert reviewers early and send them their protected-area upload links; reviews must be no more than 12 months old when you apply.
Cut the CV to two pages and the research outline to five pages, and format the publication lists exactly as the Foundation's sample lists require.
Declare every career break and child-rearing period in the application form - recognised periods can extend the four- and twelve-year windows by up to six years.
Have your doctoral certificate (or confirmation you will complete before the selection meeting) and any German language certificate ready as PDFs before the call opens.
common_rejection_risks: Formal rejection without further review for applications that omit important documents or diverge from the Foundation's specifications, such as the required publication-list format.
A slow host: the application is not forwarded to the Foundation until the host has uploaded everything, so an unresponsive host quietly ends the application.
Ambiguities that force the Foundation to ask for clarification, which usually postpone the decision to the following selection meeting and cost you a full cycle.
Returning to your doctoral supervisor or the mentor of a long earlier postdoc stay as host - generally rejected for lack of further independent academic development.
Prior Humboldt sponsorship: anyone who already held a Humboldt research fellowship or award cannot apply to this programme.
More than 90 days spent in Germany in the 18 months before the application is received, or having earned a living for more than 90 of those days from German institutional funding.
Unanimously rejected applications must wait a minimum of 18 months before re-applying.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The fellowship is a monthly income rather than a fee package and carries no tuition element, so research, conference and living costs beyond the EUR 3,000-3,600 monthly amount, the EUR 100 mobility allowance and the flat-rate travel payment must come from the host's research-costs allowance (EUR 800 per month in natural sciences, life sciences and engineering; EUR 500 per month in humanities and social sciences) or your own funds. Travel for family members is only paid in exceptional circumstances, and the partner family allowance requires your partner's monthly income in Germany to stay below EUR 603.
document_audit: The two-page CV limit and five-page research outline limit are formal requirements - overshooting them risks formal rejection without review.
Publication lists must follow the Foundation's sample lists, and for the experienced-researcher line only papers where you acted as thematic lead may be submitted as key publications.
Expert reviews must be uploaded by the reviewers themselves in the protected area; sending them by email or attaching them to your file does not count.
Key publications not in German or English need publisher acceptance notifications or acknowledgements of receipt plus summaries or translations.

If you will only complete your doctorate before the selection meeting, note that the application is formally rejected if your dissertation is unpublished and you have no further academic publications.

If bringing family: a partner must stay at least three uninterrupted months for the allowance, and marriage or partnership certificates (or children's birth certificates) are needed if entering Germany without a visa.
alerts: Calls close early: once a call reaches 800 applications it shuts, so submitting in the first weeks after a call opens matters more than the calendar date.
The decisive date is when the Foundation receives the application; if the portal closes before you submit, you keep the portal-closure date only if you submit within 14 days of the next call opening.

Career-stage windows are four years (postdocs) and twelve years (experienced researchers) after the doctorate, extendable by recognised child-rearing and career breaks up to six years; where multiple doctorates exist, the first one counts.

Research stays outside Germany are allowed only for fellowships longer than six months, cannot fall at the very beginning or end of the funding period, are capped at 25% of the total sponsorship period, and extra earnings earned abroad are deducted from the fellowship.
You cannot apply to several Humboldt fellowship programmes at the same time, and parallel applications to other funders must be declared and updated while your application is under review.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online form, get both expert reviews and the host's statement uploaded by those parties, submit while the portal is open, then wait through the formal and completeness checks, two peer reviews and a selection committee decision at the March, July or November meeting.
